mainTopic: Disqualifying witnesses: when an עד זומם loses his status, and whether a sinner who is not a money sinner can testify.
overview: The amud opens with a dispute between אביי and רבא about when an עד זומם becomes disqualified. אביי says it is למפרע, from the moment he lied. רבא says it is only מכאן ולהבא, either because הזמה is a חידוש or, in another version, to protect buyers. The הלכה follows אביי, one of the six cases of יע"ל קג"ם. Next, אביי and רבא argue about a person who eats non-kosher meat להכעיס. אביי disqualifies him as a רשע, and רבא disqualifies only a רשע דחמס, a sinner involving money. A ברייתא seems to refute אביי, and the גמרא explains how each one reads רבי מאיר's ruling about an עד זומם. The גמרא still rules like אביי. It explains that the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי, while a סתם משנה follows רבי מאיר. To show where that סתם משנה comes from, the גמרא begins the story of בר חמא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The dispute: disqualified going backward or only from now on?
steps.stepSummary: אביי says an עד זומם is disqualified למפרע. רבא says he is disqualified only מכאן ולהבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: About a conspiring witness: אביי says he is disqualified going backward in time. רבא says he is disqualified only from now on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a disagreement between אביי and רבא about when an עד זומם loses his status as a valid witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that the עד זומם is disqualified. They argue about the starting point. אביי starts it from when he testified falsely, so any testimony he gave after that is also invalid. רבא starts it only from when the second pair of witnesses exposed him.

keyTerms.meaning: A witness proven false through הזמה: other witnesses testify that he was with them somewhere else at the time of the event.
Going backward in time; retroactively.
From now and onward; not retroactive.
He becomes disqualified (from being a witness).

steps.confusionAlert: Everyone agrees that the false testimony itself is thrown out. The argument is only about other testimony he gave in the time between his false testimony and his exposure.

phrases.english: A conspiring witness:
Abaye says: he is disqualified retroactively;
phrases.notes: Retroactively means starting back from the moment he gave the false testimony, even though he was caught only later.

phrases.aramaic: וְרָבָא אָמַר: מִיכָּן וּלְהַבָּא הוּא נִפְסָל.
phrases.english: and Rava says: he is disqualified from now and onward.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵד זוֹמֵם, אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: לְמַפְרֵעַ הוּא נִפְסָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the timing of an עד זומם's disqualification.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: disqualified retroactively from the time of testimony. רבא: disqualified only from the time of exposure onward.

steps.title: אביי's reason: he became wicked when he testified
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the witness became a רשע at the moment he testified falsely, and the תורה forbids using a רשע as a witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says he is disqualified retroactively, because from the moment he testified he was a wicked person. The תורה says 'Do not put your hand with the wicked', which means: do not make a wicked person a witness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reasoning behind אביי's view, using a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, the exposure does not make him wicked. It only reveals that he already was wicked from the moment he lied. Since a רשע is unfit to testify, any testimony he gave after that moment is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: From the time that he testified.
A wicked person, who is disqualified from testifying.
Do not put / do not place.

phrases.english: Abaye says: he is disqualified retroactively,
because from the time that he testified, he is a wicked person,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַתּוֹרָה אָמְרָה: ״אַל תָּשֶׁת יָדְךָ עִם רָשָׁע״
phrases.english: and the Torah said: “Do not put your hand with the wicked”
meaning: do not set up a wicked person as a witness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: לְמַפְרֵעַ הוּא נִפְסָל, מֵעִידָּנָא דְּאַסְהֵיד רָשָׁע הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of the dispute in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's ruling that the disqualification is retroactive.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 23:1, ״אל תשת ידך עם רשע״, read as 'do not make a רשע a witness.'

steps.title: רבא's reason: the law of a conspiring witness is a novelty
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that הזמה goes against normal logic (a חידוש), so it takes effect only from the time the witnesses are exposed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says he is disqualified only from now on. The law of an עד זומם is a novelty. What makes you rely on these witnesses? Rely on those! So you can apply it to him only from the time of its novelty and onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reasoning behind רבא's view: the law of הזמה is unusual, so we limit it to the moment it actually happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when two witnesses contradict two other witnesses, we cannot know who is telling the truth. The תורה nevertheless tells us to believe the second pair against the first, and that is the חידוש. Since this rule goes beyond plain logic, רבא applies it only from the moment of the הזמה and not backward.

keyTerms.meaning: A novelty: a law that goes against normal logic and is accepted only because the תורה says so.
What did you see? That is, what reason do you have to prefer this side?
Rely on.
From the time its novelty takes effect and onward.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר: מִיכָּן וּלְהַבָּא הוּא נִפְסָל.
phrases.english: Rava says: he is disqualified from now and onward.
A conspiring witness is a novelty,
what did you see that you rely on these?
phrases.notes: “These” are the second pair, who say the first pair was with them somewhere else.

phrases.english: Rely on those!
phrases.notes: “Those” are the first pair, who testified about the event.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָךְ בּוֹ אֶלָּא מִשְּׁעַת חִידּוּשׁוֹ וְאֵילָךְ.
phrases.english: You have him only from the time of its novelty and onward.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מִיכָּן וּלְהַבָּא הוּא נִפְסָל. עֵד זוֹמֵם חִידּוּשׁ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second side of the dispute, in contrast to אביי's reasoning in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because הזמה is a חידוש, its disqualification applies only from the moment of הזמה onward.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general principle: a law that is a חידוש is applied narrowly and not stretched further than it has to be.

steps.title: Another version: רבא really agrees with אביי
steps.stepSummary: An איכא דאמרי version says that רבא agrees with אביי in principle that the witness is a רשע from the time he testified.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבא also holds like אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רבא's opinion. In this version, רבא agrees with אביי's basic idea, which sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the argument about the חידוש is dropped. רבא agrees that in principle the witness was a רשע from the time of his testimony. This raises an obvious puzzle: why does רבא still rule 'from now on'?

keyTerms.meaning: Also.
He holds (this opinion).

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rava also holds like Abaye,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: רָבָא נָמֵי כְּאַבַּיֵּי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reasoning of step 3 with a different understanding of רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In principle, רבא agrees that the עד זומם is a רשע from the time he testified.

steps.title: So why does רבא say 'from now on'?
steps.stepSummary: If רבא agrees with אביי, the גמרא asks why he rules that the disqualification starts only from now on.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is the reason he says 'from now and onward'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question so that it can explain רבא's ruling in this second version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבא now agrees with אביי's reasoning, his practical ruling seems to contradict his own view. The גמרא needs a new, separate reason for it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
He says.

phrases.english: And what is the reason he says “from now and onward”?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 4: if רבא agrees in principle, why does he still rule differently?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for רבא's 'from now on' ruling, given that he agrees with אביי in principle.

steps.title: To protect buyers from losing money
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules 'from now on' only to protect buyers whose purchases were confirmed by this witness before he was exposed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the loss to buyers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא's ruling is a practical protection for buyers, not a disagreement about the basic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the disqualification went backward, every sale this witness signed on in the meantime would become invalid. Innocent buyers would then lose what they bought. So in this version רבא agrees with אביי's logic but limits the practical effect to avoid that harm.

keyTerms.meaning: Loss.
Buyers; purchasers.

steps.whatToRemember: First version: אביי says למפרע because he became a רשע when he testified, and רבא says מכאן ולהבא because הזמה is a חידוש. Second version: רבא agrees with אביי in principle and says מכאן ולהבא only to protect buyers from loss.

phrases.english: Because of the loss to buyers.
phrases.notes: He means buyers whose purchase documents this witness signed during the time before he was exposed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא limits the disqualification to 'from now on' to prevent losses to buyers whose transactions this witness validated.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two versions of רבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two explanations of רבא's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the next step: in what case would the two explanations of רבא give different rulings?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both versions רבא rules that the witness is disqualified only from now on. The only difference is the reason: either הזמה is a חידוש, or he wants to protect buyers. The גמרא wants to know when that difference in reason changes the actual ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: "Them" means the two versions of רבא's reason from the earlier steps: a חידוש, or protecting buyers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the reason given in step 3 with the reason given in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two explanations of רבא lead to different rulings.

steps.title: Two cases where the two versions of רבא differ
steps.stepSummary: The versions differ when each witness is refuted by a separate pair of witnesses, or when the witnesses are disqualified for robbery.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them when two witnesses testified about one of the witnesses, and two others about the other. Or also, when they disqualified the witnesses by showing they were robbers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two cases where the two explanations of רבא lead to different rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the witnesses lose their status, but not through regular הזמה. If רבא's reason is that הזמה is a חידוש, the 'from now on' rule applies only to real הזמה, so here the witness is disqualified from the time he sinned. If the reason is protecting buyers, that concern exists in every case, so here too the disqualification starts only from now on.

keyTerms.meaning: They testified
Two witnesses about one witness
Alternatively; or also
Robbery; being a robber

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא changes his mind here. In both versions רבא says 'from now on' for a regular עד זומם. The question is only whether that rule also covers other ways of disqualifying a witness.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where two testified about one
phrases.notes: Each original witness is refuted by his own separate pair, not both together. So it is not ordinary הזמה.

phrases.english: Or also,
where they disqualified them through robbery

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Cases of disqualification that are not regular הזמה. Under the חידוש reason they are retroactive; under the buyer-protection reason they are only from now on.

steps.title: רב פפי ruled in practice like רבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה from דיפתי reports that רב פפי decided an actual case following רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ירמיה from דיפתי said: רב פפי decided an actual case following רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from theory to practice and reports a real court ruling that followed רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An actual ruling (עובדא) carries great weight, because it shows how a judge decided a real case. Here it supports רבא: the עד זומם is disqualified only from the time he was exposed.

keyTerms.meaning: He ruled on an actual case
Following him; in agreement with him
From דיפתי, a town in Babylonia

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya of Difti said:
Rav Pappi performed an action
phrases.notes: This means he actually decided a real case in court.

phrases.english: in accordance with Rava

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲבַד רַב פַּפִּי עוֹבָדָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from explaining רבא to how the dispute was actually decided.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, רב פפי ruled like רבא: the disqualification starts from now on.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי rules like אביי
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי disagrees and says the הלכה follows אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: the הלכה follows אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: A later authority gives the opposite ruling: the הלכה is like אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the עד זומם is disqualified retroactively, from the moment he testified falsely. Testimony he gave in between is invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: The final practical law

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
The halakha is in accordance with Abaye

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the practical ruling reported in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה is like אביי: an עד זומם is disqualified retroactively.

steps.title: The הלכה follows אביי in the six cases of יע"ל קג"ם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that the הלכה follows אביי in the cases remembered by the sign יע"ל קג"ם, and our case is one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows אביי in the cases of יע"ל קג"ם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the matter. Usually the הלכה follows רבא over אביי, but here it follows אביי, because this is one of the six cases in the famous memory sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule is that the הלכה follows רבא when he argues with אביי, except in six cases. The letter ע in יע"ל קג"ם stands for עד זומם, the case we have been learning. So the final ruling is that the עד זומם is disqualified retroactively.

keyTerms.meaning: Memory sign for the six cases where the הלכה follows אביי
A memory aid made of letters
A witness exposed by הזמה; the ע of the sign

steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: like אביי, an עד זומם is disqualified from the moment he testified falsely. This is the ע in יע"ל קג"ם, one of the six exceptions to the rule that the הלכה follows רבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: The sign יע"ל קג"ם is used throughout ש"ס. It reminds us that in almost every dispute between אביי and רבא the הלכה follows רבא, except in these six cases.

phrases.english: And the halakha is in accordance with Abaye
in "Ya'al Kagam"
phrases.notes: A memory sign: יאוש, עד זומם, לחי, קידושין, גילוי דעת בגט, מומר. Our case is the ע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms step 10 and explains why the usual rule of following רבא does not apply here.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows אביי: an עד זומם is disqualified retroactively, one of the six cases of יע"ל קג"ם.

steps.title: A מומר who eats נבילות out of appetite is disqualified by all
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: everyone agrees that a person who eats non-kosher meat because he wants it is disqualified as a witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: A sinner who eats נבילות because of his appetite: everyone agrees he is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion about who is disqualified as a witness. It starts with the case everyone agrees on, to set up a dispute that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who breaks the תורה just to satisfy his desire might also lie in court for his own benefit, so he is unfit to testify. By saying 'everyone agrees' about this case, the גמרא signals that the following case, a different kind of מומר, will be argued about.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who regularly breaks a specific law of the תורה
Meat of animals that were not properly slaughtered
Out of appetite; because he desires it
Everyone agrees
Disqualified, here from being a witness

phrases.english: A transgressor who eats carcasses
due to appetite
everyone agrees he is disqualified

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּמָר אוֹכֵל נְבֵילוֹת לְתֵיאָבוֹן דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new dispute between אביי and רבא about disqualifying witnesses, after the עד זומם discussion was settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מומר לתיאבון for eating נבילות is disqualified as a witness according to everyone.

steps.title: Eating non-kosher meat out of spite: a dispute
steps.stepSummary: אביי says someone who eats non-kosher meat להכעיס is פסול to be a witness. רבא says he is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he eats it to provoke (out of spite): אביי says he is disqualified, and רבא says he is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the agreed case (eating because he wants it) to the case people argue about: eating it just to show defiance. אביי and רבא disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who eats out of desire is clearly disqualified. A person who eats להכעיס is not driven by temptation. He is openly rejecting the תורה. The question is whether that kind of sinner is also disqualified from being a witness.

keyTerms.meaning: To provoke or anger; doing a sin out of spite, not because he wants it
Disqualified (here, from being a witness)
Fit, valid (here, allowed to be a witness)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume להכעיס is the 'lighter' case. Many would see it as worse than eating out of desire. רבא's point is about what kind of sin disqualifies a witness, not about which sin is worse.

phrases.english: To provoke (out of spite) –
אביי says: he is disqualified,
רבא says: he is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְהַכְעִיס – אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: פָּסוּל, רָבָא אָמַר: כָּשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the agreed case from step 12 and presents the disputed version of it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: one who eats non-kosher meat להכעיס is פסול לעדות. רבא: he is כשר.

steps.title: The reasons behind each opinion
steps.stepSummary: אביי disqualifies him because he is a רשע, and the פסוק says not to make a רשע a witness. רבא says only a רשע דחמס, a sinner involving money, is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says he is disqualified because he is a wicked person, and the Torah says, 'Do not put a wicked person as a witness.' רבא says he is fit, because we need a wicked person of חמס (a sinner involving money).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each one holds his view. Both build on the same פסוק but read it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (שמות 23:1) says אל תשת ידך עם רשע להיות עד חמס. אביי focuses on the word רשע, so any wicked person is out. רבא reads רשע together with חמס, so only someone whose wickedness involves money, like a thief, is disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: A wicked person
'The Merciful One,' a name for ה׳ / the תורה
Wrongdoing involving money, like robbery
We require

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core definition question: does any open sinner lose his credibility as a witness, or only someone who sins for money?

phrases.english: אביי says: he is disqualified,
because he is a wicked person,
and the Merciful One said:
"Do not put a wicked person as a witness."
phrases.notes: שמות 23:1, read here as 'don't make a רשע into a witness.'

phrases.english: And רבא says: he is fit,
we require a wicked person of חמס.
phrases.notes: The word חמס comes from the end of the same פסוק: 'עד חמס.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: פָּסוּל, דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ רָשָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning and source for each side of the dispute in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: any רשע is disqualified, based on 'אל תשת רשע עד.' רבא: only a רשע דחמס (monetary sinner) is disqualified.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to disqualify even non-money oath breakers
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the פסוק disqualifies thieves and people who are מועלין בשבועות. The גמרא suggests this includes even a שבועת שוא, which has nothing to do with money. That would go against רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: '"Do not put a wicked person as a witness," "Do not put a חמס person as a witness" – these are robbers and those who betray oaths.' Doesn't this mean both a false oath that is pointless and a false oath about money?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack רבא. It argues that 'oath breakers' must include a person who swears falsely about something that has nothing to do with money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שבועת שוא, like swearing that a stone is a stone, involves no money at all. If that person is disqualified, then a sinner who is not a רשע דחמס is also disqualified. That contradicts רבא and supports אביי. The plural word שבועות hints at more than one type of oath.

keyTerms.meaning: Robbers
Those who betray (break) oaths, swearing falsely
A pointless or false oath with no money involved
An oath about money, like denying a debt

phrases.english: They challenged:
"Do not put a wicked person as a witness,"
"Do not put a person of חמס as a witness" –
these are robbers
and those who betray oaths.
Is it not that it means
both a pointless oath
and an oath about money?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's reasoning from step 14 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that only a רשע דחמס is disqualified.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא disqualifies מועלין בשבועות in the plural, which seems to include שבועת שוא. That oath involves no money, so a non-monetary sinner would be disqualified.

steps.title: The ברייתא means only oaths about money
steps.stepSummary: No. Both kinds the ברייתא means are שבועת ממון. The plural שבועות just means oaths in general.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, both this and that are oaths about money. And why does it say 'oaths' (plural)? It means oaths in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא. It says the ברייתא is talking only about false oaths involving money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'oath breakers' refers only to שבועת ממון, those people are really a kind of רשע דחמס, which fits רבא. The plural word does not point to two types of oaths. It is just a general way of speaking about oaths that come up in money matters.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that, both cases
In general, of the world

steps.whatToRemember: אביי disqualifies anyone who sins להכעיס because he is a רשע. רבא disqualifies only a רשע דחמס. The ברייתא about מועלין בשבועות does not disprove רבא, because it means only oaths about money.

phrases.english: No, both this and that are oaths about money.
And what is meant by "oaths" (plural)?
Oaths in general.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 and saves רבא's position.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא: 'oaths' refers only to monetary oaths.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מועלין בשבועות includes שבועת שוא, so even non-monetary sinners are disqualified.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both oaths in the ברייתא are שבועת ממון. The plural just means oaths generally, so the ברייתא fits רבא.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the disqualified רשע is a money sinner
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוק as disqualifying a רשע who is a חמס, robbers and lenders with interest. That suggests only money sinners are disqualified, which goes against אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'Do not set a רשע as a witness; do not set a person of חמס as a witness.' These are robbers and people who lend with interest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to attack אביי. It says the רשע the פסוק disqualifies is a רשע of חמס, meaning money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא ties the word רשע to the word חמס, which means money wrongdoing. Its examples, robbers and lenders with interest, are all money sins. That fits רבא's view that only a רשע דחמס is disqualified, so it challenges אביי, who disqualifies a person who eats non-kosher meat להכעיס.

keyTerms.meaning: Wrongdoing involving money or property
Robbers
People who lend money with interest

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
'Do not set a wicked person as a witness,'
'do not set a person of money wrongdoing as a witness.'
These are robbers and people who lend with interest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge to רבא was answered in Step 16, the גמרא now attacks אביי.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's ruling that someone who eats non-kosher meat להכעיס is פסול לעדות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא defines the disqualified רשע as a רשע דחמס and gives only money sinners as examples, so a sinner whose sin has nothing to do with money is not included.

steps.title: אביי is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares that the challenge to אביי stands. His view is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The refutation of אביי is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the challenge by saying אביי has no answer. His view is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תיובתא means a full refutation, not just a question. The ברייתא clearly limits the disqualified רשע to money sinners, so רבא's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation that has no answer, so the view is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא seems to show that only a רשע דחמס, a money sinner, is disqualified, so אביי is refuted for now. Step 23 rules like אביי anyway, and Step 25 explains that this ברייתא follows רבי יוסי.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up תיובתא with קשיא. A קשיא is a question that might get an answer. A תיובתא means the view is knocked down.
steps.whyThisMatters: For now רבא's view stands. Step 23 rules like אביי anyway, and steps 24–27 explain how that ruling can survive this refutation.

phrases.english: The refutation of אביי is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Declares that the challenge in Step 17 succeeded.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי is refuted by this ברייתא. Steps 23–27 later rule like him, because the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי and a סתם משנה follows רבי מאיר.

steps.title: A מחלוקת תנאים about an עד זומם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests linking אביי and רבא to a מחלוקת תנאים. רבי מאיר says an עד זומם is disqualified for every kind of case. רבי יוסי says that is only true if he was proven a זומם in a capital case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say it is like a מחלוקת תנאים: an עד זומם is disqualified for the entire Torah; these are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יוסי says: when is this said? When he was proven a זומם in a capital case. But if he was proven a זומם in a money case, he is still valid for capital cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes a מחלוקת תנאים that it will try to match to אביי and רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that once a witness is caught lying in any kind of case, he is disqualified for all cases. רבי יוסי holds that lying in a money case does not disqualify him for capital cases. A lie in a capital case does disqualify him for everything.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say this is like a מחלוקת between תנאים
A witness proven to have lied, by other witnesses who say he was somewhere else
Capital cases, about life and death
Money cases
He was proven an עד זומם

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute of תנאים:
A conspiring witness is disqualified
for the entire Torah,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.
רבי יוסי says:
When is this said?
When he was proven a lying witness in a capital case;
but if he was proven a lying witness in a money case,
he is valid for capital cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי is refuted, the גמרא looks for a מחלוקת תנאים that matches the argument between אביי and רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: an עד זומם is disqualified for all cases. רבי יוסי: a זומם in a money case is still valid for capital cases.

steps.title: Suggesting אביי follows רבי מאיר and רבא follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that אביי holds like רבי מאיר, who lets a disqualification spread from a lighter area to a more serious one. רבא holds like רבי יוסי, who lets it spread only from a serious area to a lighter one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that אביי holds like רבי מאיר and רבא like רבי יוסי? אביי is like רבי מאיר, who says we do reason from a lighter case to a more serious case. רבא is like רבי יוסי, who says we reason from a serious case to a lighter case, but not from a lighter case to a more serious case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out its suggestion. It says אביי matches רבי מאיר and רבא matches רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both arguments ask the same thing: does being disqualified in one area carry over to a different area? רבי מאיר says it carries over even to a more serious area, and that would fit אביי. רבי יוסי says it carries over only to a lighter area, and that would fit רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: From a lighter case to a more serious case
From a serious case to a lighter case
We say, meaning we use this reasoning

phrases.english: Shall we say: אביי holds like רבי מאיר,
and רבא like רבי יוסי?
אביי is like רבי מאיר, who says:
we do reason from a lighter case to a more serious one.
And רבא, who ruled like רבי יוסי,
who says: from a serious case to a lighter one we reason,
from a lighter case to a more serious one we do not reason.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא: אַבָּיֵי כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְרָבָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the suggestion from Step 19 by matching each אמורא to a תנא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the מחלוקת between אביי and רבא the same as the מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי?

steps.title: No, the argument is only about רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Under רבי יוסי's view, אביי and רבא agree. They argue only about how to understand רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. According to רבי יוסי, everyone agrees. Where they disagree is according to רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own suggestion. אביי and רבא do not have to be split between the two תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי יוסי, both אביי and רבא would agree that a disqualification does not spread from a lighter area to a more serious one. Their argument is about how far רבי מאיר's rule reaches. So the argument between אביי and רבא is not the same as the argument between the תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of
Everyone agrees
Where they do disagree

steps.whatToRemember: The suggestion that אביי follows רבי מאיר and רבא follows רבי יוסי is rejected. According to רבי יוסי, both אביי and רבא would agree that the sinner is not disqualified. Their argument is only about how to read רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: No.
According to רבי יוסי
everyone agrees and does not argue,
phrases.notes: Everyone here means אביי and רבא.

phrases.english: where they disagree is according to רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא. אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the match proposed in Step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that אביי and רבא match the two תנאים. It does not reject either תנא's ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumed אביי could not hold like רבי יוסי. In fact both אמוראים agree with רבי יוסי's view and argue only about רבי מאיר.

steps.title: How אביי and רבא each read רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: אביי follows רבי מאיר fully. רבא says רבי מאיר spoke only about an עד זומם in a money case, who harmed both Heaven and people. A person who only sinned against Heaven is not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי holds like רבי מאיר. רבא says: רבי מאיר only said his rule there, about a false witness in a money case, because that person is bad to Heaven and bad to people. But here, where the person is bad to Heaven but not bad to people, רבי מאיר would not disqualify him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in the claim from the last step that אביי and רבא only argue about רבי מאיר. It shows exactly how each one reads him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי takes רבי מאיר's rule and applies it to a person who sins against Heaven. רבא limits רבי מאיר to an עד זומם in a money case. That witness lied to Heaven and also hurt another person's pocket. Someone who sinned only against Heaven, like one who eats non-kosher meat to rebel, has not shown he will cheat people, so even רבי מאיר would not disqualify him.

keyTerms.meaning: "Until here he only said": he said his rule only in this case
A witness proven false because other witnesses show he was somewhere else
Bad toward Heaven: a sin against God
Bad toward people: harming other human beings

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing with רבי מאיר. He agrees with רבי מאיר and just reads his rule more narrowly than אביי does.

phrases.english: Abaye holds like Rabbi Meir,

phrases.aramaic: וְרָבָא: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר
phrases.english: and Rava says: Rabbi Meir only said his rule

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם אֶלָּא גַּבֵּי עֵד זוֹמֵם דְּמָמוֹן,
phrases.english: there, regarding a false (zomem) witness in a money case,
who is bad toward Heaven and bad toward people.
But here, where he is bad toward Heaven
phrases.notes: "Here" is the person who eats non-kosher meat just to rebel.

phrases.english: and not bad toward people, no, he is not disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the claim in Step 21 that אביי and רבא argue only about how to read רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a תנא's ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that רבא must disagree with רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא can agree with רבי מאיר, because רבי מאיר's rule covers only someone who is bad to Heaven and also bad to people.

steps.title: The הלכה follows אביי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה follows אביי: someone who sins against Heaven is disqualified as a witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is like אביי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a practical ruling: we follow אביי. The next steps will test whether this ruling holds up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising, because in Step 18 אביי's view was refuted. Ruling for a view that was refuted sets up the challenge that comes right after.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows his view

steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the few famous cases where the הלכה follows אביי against רבא.

phrases.english: And the halacha is like Abaye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After laying out both views, the גמרא decides between them.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, one who sins against Heaven (like eating non-kosher meat to rebel) is disqualified as a witness.

steps.title: But אביי was refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we can rule like אביי when his view was already refuted by a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't אביי refuted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling it just gave. It reminds us that אביי's view was knocked down earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Steps 17 and 18, a ברייתא said that only a money sinner (חמס) is disqualified, and the גמרא declared אביי refuted. Normally a refuted view cannot become the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: He was refuted (his view was knocked down by a source)

phrases.english: But wasn't he refuted?
phrases.notes: This points back to the ברייתא about the רשע who is a חמס, from a few steps ago.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the הלכה follows אביי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A view that was refuted by a ברייתא cannot be the הלכה.

steps.title: That ברייתא follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that refuted אביי follows רבי יוסי. אביי follows רבי מאיר, so that ברייתא does not bind him.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ברייתא is the view of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ברייתא that refuted אביי represents only רבי יוסי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא showed that under רבי יוסי, אביי and רבא agree. So the ברייתא fits רבי יוסי. אביי, however, follows רבי מאיר, so the ברייתא is no longer a refutation of him. It is just the other side of a מחלוקת תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: That one: that source

phrases.english: That ברייתא is Rabbi Yosei's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to one side of a dispute between תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be the law for everyone, which would refute אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי only. אביי follows רבי מאיר.

steps.title: But the halacha follows רבי יוסי over רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: Even if the ברייתא is רבי יוסי, there is a general rule: when רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי. So how can we rule like אביי?
steps.simpleTranslation: So let it be רבי יוסי! When רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue, the הלכה is like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Saying the ברייתא is רבי יוסי makes things worse for אביי, not better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a set rule for deciding between these two תנאים: we follow רבי יוסי. If אביי depends on רבי מאיר, then the הלכה should go against אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: And let it even be: so what if it is?
The law follows רבי יוסי (in his disputes with רבי מאיר)

phrases.english: So what if it is Rabbi Yosei?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי – הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי!
phrases.english: When Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei argue, the halacha follows Rabbi Yosei!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling like אביי, now that it rests on רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the rules for deciding the law, רבי יוסי beats רבי מאיר, so the ruling should go against אביי.

steps.title: An unattributed משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: This case is different. A סתם משנה (a משנה with no name attached) follows רבי מאיר, and a סתם משנה decides the law.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the תנא taught us an unattributed משנה like רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Here a special rule overrides the usual one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we follow רבי יוסי over רבי מאיר. But when a משנה states the law with no name attached, that is a sign the law follows that view. Since such a משנה follows רבי מאיר here, the הלכה is like רבי מאיר, and so like אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there: this case has a special reason
The תנא taught us without naming anyone, as a plain ruling

phrases.english: It is different there,
because the Tanna taught us a plain, unnamed ruling like Rabbi Meir.
phrases.notes: When a משנה gives a ruling with no name on it, we usually treat that ruling as the law.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דִּסְתַם לַן תְּנָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A stronger rule for deciding the law overrides the general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The general rule should apply: we follow רבי יוסי over רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: A סתם משנה like רבי מאיר overrides that general rule, so the הלכה follows רבי מאיר and אביי.

steps.title: Where is that unattributed משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the סתם משנה that follows רבי מאיר is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where did the תנא teach us this unnamed ruling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind its last answer. This sets up the next step, where it will point to the actual משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole defense of אביי now depends on a סתם משנה following רבי מאיר. So the גמרא has to show that such a משנה really exists.

keyTerms.meaning: And where?

phrases.english: And where did he teach us this unnamed ruling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the answer in Step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The location of the unattributed משנה that follows רבי מאיר

steps.title: בר חמא kills a person and the ריש גלותא orders an investigation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a story: בר חמא killed someone, and the ריש גלותא told רב אבא בר יעקב to investigate and, if the killing was certain, to blind him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like the case of בר חמא, who killed a person. The ריש גלותא said to רב אבא בר יעקב: Go investigate this. If he definitely killed, let them put out his eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering where the סתם משנה like רבי מאיר is found, by telling a real-life story in which it came up. This step only sets the scene.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is וַדַּאי, meaning "certainly." The punishment depends on the killing being clearly proven. That is why the next steps focus on witnesses and whether their testimony can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, the leader of the Jewish community in בבל
Go out and investigate it
Certainly, definitely
Let them put out his eyes

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּבַר חָמָא קְטַל נַפְשָׁא,
phrases.english: Like that case in which bar Chama killed a person.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא לְרַב אַבָּא בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: The Exilarch said to Rav Abba bar Yaakov:
Go out and investigate it.
If he certainly killed,
let them put out his eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּבַר חָמָא קְטַל נַפְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 28's question about where the סתם משנה following רבי מאיר is found, by telling the incident in which it came up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If בר חמא certainly killed, he is to be blinded.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer comes through the story of בר חמא; the story continues past this step and leads to the source of the סתם משנה.

steps.title: Two witnesses testify that he certainly killed
steps.stepSummary: Two witnesses came and testified that בר חמא definitely committed the killing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two witnesses came and testified about him that he definitely killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. Two witnesses supply exactly the proof the ריש גלותא asked for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses are the standard full proof. Their words, וַדַּאי קְטַל, match the condition set in the previous step, so the punishment should now apply unless the witnesses are disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: Two witnesses
They testified

phrases.english: Two witnesses came,
and testified about him that he certainly killed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: the condition of certain killing now appears to be met.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two witnesses testify that the killing definitely happened.

steps.title: בר חמא brings witnesses claiming one witness is a thief
steps.stepSummary: בר חמא brought two witnesses who testified that one of the first witnesses stole. The first said he stole a קב of barley, and the second begins to describe a theft as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and brought two witnesses, and they testified about one of those witnesses. One said: In front of me he stole a קב of barley. And one said: In front of me he stole...
steps.whatsHappening: בר חמא fights back by trying to show that one of the witnesses against him is a thief. The amud ends in the middle of the second witness's words, and the story continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thief cannot serve as a witness. If one of the two murder witnesses is disqualified, the proof against בר חמא falls apart. Each of the new witnesses saw a separate theft, and that detail sets up the legal question that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of me, in my presence
He stole
A קב, a measure of volume
Barley

phrases.english: He went and brought two witnesses,
phrases.notes: "He" is בר חמא, the accused killer.

phrases.english: who testified about one of those witnesses.

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: קַמַּאי דִּידִי גְּנַב קַבָּא דְחוּשְׁלָא,
phrases.english: One said: He stole a kav of barley in front of me,
and one said: He stole in front of me

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The accused responds to the witnesses of step 30 by trying to disqualify one of them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two witnesses claim that one of the murder witnesses is a thief, but each of them describes a separate theft.
